questions.question: In a queueing system, job $k$ arrives at time $A_k$, waits $W_k$ in the queue, receives service of length $S_k$ and departs at time $D_k$. Which quantity is its sojourn time $J_k$?
options: $J_k=D_k-A_k-S_k$, the time spent queueing before service starts
$J_k=D_k-A_k$, the whole time from arrival until departure
$J_k=D_k-A_{k-1}$, the time since the previous job arrived
$J_k=S_k$, the time the server spends working on job $k$

questions.question: For a job $k$ with waiting time $W_k\geq0$ in the queue and service time $S_k$, how does its sojourn time $J_k$ compare with $S_k$?
options: $J_k\leq S_k$, with equality exactly when the queue is empty at $A_k$
$J_k\geq S_k$, with equality exactly when the server is idle at $D_k$
$J_k\geq S_k$, with equality exactly when the job does not wait
$J_k$ and $S_k$ can be ordered either way, depending on $W_k$

questions.question: Job $k$ arrives at $A_k$ and departs at $D_k>A_k$. With the presence indicator $I_k(s)=\mathbf{1}\{A_k\leq s<D_k\}$, what is $\int_0^\infty I_k(s)\,\mathrm{d}s$?
options: The value $1$, since $I_k$ is an indicator
The waiting time $W_k$ of job $k$ in the queue
The number of jobs in the system at time $A_k$

questions.question: Jobs $k=1,2,\dots$ have presence indicators $I_k(s)=\mathbf{1}\{A_k\leq s<D_k\}$, where $A_k$ and $D_k$ are arrival and departure times. What does the sum $\sum_k I_k(s)$ equal at a fixed time $s$?
options: The total sojourn time $\sum_k J_k$ of all jobs
The number of jobs in service at time $s$
The number $L(s)$ of jobs in the system at time $s$

questions.question: Along a sample path of $n$ jobs with sojourn times $J_1,\dots,J_n$, the average $\bar{J}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=1}^{n}J_k$ is compared with the time-average number in system $\bar{L}$. What kind of average is $\bar{J}$?
options: A time average, like $\bar{L}$, because sojourn times are measured in time units
A time average over $[0,D_n]$, obtained by dividing $\sum_k J_k$ by $D_n$
An arrival average: each job counts once, whatever its length of stay
An average over service completions only, so idle periods lower it

questions.question: A job arrives at time $A_k=3$, waits $W_k=5$ in the queue and then receives service of length $S_k=2$. At what time $D_k$ does it depart?
At a single FIFO server, the arrival counting process $A(t)$ jumps at times $1,2,5$ and the departure counting process $D(t)$ jumps at times $4,6,7$. What is the sojourn time $J_2$ of the second job?
Job $k-1$ at a single FIFO server has sojourn time $J_{k-1}=2$. Job $k$ arrives $X_k=5$ time units after job $k-1$ and needs service $S_k=4$. Using $J_k=[J_{k-1}-X_k]^+ +S_k$, find $J_k$.

A queue starts empty at time $0$; $4$ jobs arrive and the last one departs at time $10$, after which the system is empty. The area under the number-in-system curve is $\int_0^{10}L(s)\,\mathrm{d}s=12$. What is the average sojourn time $\bar{J}$ of the $4$ jobs?
A job departs at time $D_k=15$ after a sojourn time $J_k=7$, of which $S_k=3$ is its service time. At what time did its service start?
At a single FIFO server that works at rate one whenever jobs are present, why is the workload just after job $k$ arrives equal to its sojourn time $J_k$?
options: Job $k$ leaves once all work present just after $A_k$, its own $S_k$ included, is done
The workload just after $A_k$ equals the service time $S_k$ of job $k$, and $J_k=S_k$ under FIFO
The workload just after $A_k$ counts the jobs present, and each present job adds one unit to $J_k$
The workload just after $A_k$ equals the waiting time $W_k$, and $W_k=J_k$ for a single server

questions.question: For one sample path, $A(t)$ and $D(t)$ count the arrivals and departures up to time $t$. Which statement about the horizontal distance at height $k$ between $A(t)$ and $D(t)$, and the area between the curves, is correct?
options: Both readings need FIFO: without it, neither the distance is $J_k$ nor the area $\sum_k J_k$
Under FIFO the distance is $J_k$; under other orders it may not be, but the area still equals $\sum_k J_k$
For any service order the distance is $J_k$, because the $k$-th arrival is always the $k$-th departure
Under FIFO the distance is the waiting time $W_k$, and the area equals $\sum_k W_k$

questions.question: At a single FIFO server, job $k$ arrives $X_k$ time units after job $k-1$, whose sojourn time is $J_{k-1}$. When $J_{k-1}-X_k>0$, what does this difference measure?
options: The idle time of the server between the departure of job $k-1$ and the arrival of job $k$
The remaining service time of job $k-1$ only, excluding any time job $k-1$ spends queueing
The sojourn time $J_k$ of job $k$, because job $k$ leaves when job $k-1$ has left
The time from the arrival of job $k$ until job $k-1$ departs, which is the waiting time $W_k$

questions.question: A single FIFO server is empty at time $0$. Three jobs arrive at $A=(0,2,3)$ with service times $S=(3,1,2)$, and the last one departs at $D_3=6$. What is the time-average number in system $\bar{L}$ on $[0,6]$?
A single FIFO server uses $J_k=[J_{k-1}-X_k]^+ +S_k$ with $J_0=0$. The inter-arrival times are $X=(0,1,1)$ (the first job arrives at time $0$) and the service times are $S=(4,2,3)$. What is $J_3$?
For a sample path of $4$ jobs, the sojourn times add up to $\sum_{k=1}^{4}J_k=20$ and the service times add up to $\sum_{k=1}^{4}S_k=8$. What is the average waiting time $\bar{W}$ in the queue?
At a single FIFO server, $J_k=[J_{k-1}-X_k]^+ +S_k$ with inter-arrival time $X_k$ and service time $S_k>0$. Which condition is both necessary and sufficient for $J_k=S_k$?
options: $J_{k-1}<X_k$: job $k-1$ leaves strictly before job $k$ arrives
$S_{k-1}\leq X_k$: job $k-1$'s service fits in the inter-arrival time
$J_{k-1}\leq X_k$: job $k-1$ has left by the time job $k$ arrives

questions.question: A single FIFO server starts empty. A path is cut off at the departure time $D_n$ of job $n$, and job $n+1$ arrives at $A_{n+1}<D_n$. How do $\int_0^{D_n}L(s)\,\mathrm{d}s$ and $\sum_{k=1}^{n}J_k$ compare?
options: The integral is strictly larger, since job $n+1$ is present on $[A_{n+1},D_n)$
They are equal, since jobs $1,\dots,n$ have all left by $D_n$ under FIFO
The integral is strictly smaller, since job $n$ is cut off at $D_n$
The integral is larger by exactly $J_{n+1}$, the full stay of job $n+1$

questions.question: A single server serves without interruption and, when it becomes free, picks the most recently arrived waiting job (last-in-first-out). Jobs $1,2,3$ arrive at $A=(0,1,2)$ with service times $S=(3,1,1)$. What is the sojourn time $J_2$ of job $2$?

Two identical servers work in parallel. Job $1$ arrives at time $0$ with service time $S_1=5$; job $2$ arrives at time $1$ with $S_2=1$. What is the actual sojourn time $J_2$, given that the formula $J_k=[J_{k-1}-X_k]^+ +S_k$ is derived for one FIFO server?
